solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Queen backed landlady becoming politician!

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the royal abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen
a publican runs a pub, as a landlady does

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a pub landlady has gone into politics with royal support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the royal abbreviation round. A republican wants no monarch at all, which makes the royal backing in the surface ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: A republican is a supporter of rule without a monarch, and in the US a member of one of the two main parties.

clue.text: Knocked loudly, entranced

indicators.note: loudly means out loud, so the word for knocked is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to have rapped is to have knocked sharply

explanation.surface: Someone hammering on a door while totally spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' tells you to say RAPPED out loud; it sounds just like the word for spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rapt is completely absorbed or spellbound, the same state as being entranced.

clue.text: Sentences prisoner finally, in stages

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the word for stages

parts.note: phases are stages in a process

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word prisoner

explanation.surface: A convict serving out jail terms in stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentences' suggests prison terms, backed up by 'prisoner', but it is the definition in its grammatical sense. The R from 'prisoner finally' goes inside PHASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrases are groups of words, and the plural noun stands loosely for sentences as units of speech.

clue.text: Spread caresses for a clumsy person

parts.note: butter is a spread for bread
to finger something is to touch or stroke it, so fingers can mean caresses

explanation.surface: Applying butter and stroking something, as advice for someone clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' and 'caresses' look like verbs in a sentence but give a noun and a verb that join into the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfingers is a jokey idiom for someone who keeps dropping things, as if their hands were greasy.

clue.text: Firing it in going off without finishing

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, signalling these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: without finishing means the last letter of going is dropped

explanation.surface: Something firing up even though the engine is running without finishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going without finishing' gives GOIN, and 'off' rearranges it with the two short words before it. 'in' looks like a link word placing one thing inside another, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignition is the act of setting fuel alight, which is what firing an engine or charge means.

clue.text: A good ground halved trouble

indicators.note: halved keeps only the first half of the word ground

explanation.surface: A football pitch cut in half is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground halved' keeps the first three of its six letters, GRO. AGGRO is British slang for aggressive trouble-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang, short for aggravation, meaning hostility or violent trouble.

clue.text: Buckle quietly after fighting

indicators.note: after puts the letter for quietly behind the word for fighting

parts.note: war is fighting on a large scale
P, piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A belt buckle working loose silently after a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckle' looks like the fastening, but it is the verb meaning to bend out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To warp is to bend or twist out of shape, which is what metal does when it buckles.

clue.text: Poison from caries treated with nitrogen

indicators.note: treated suggests something processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A dentist warns that tooth decay treated with nitrogen gives off something toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: The N from 'nitrogen' joins CARIES and all six plus one are rearranged, which is why it lands in the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a famously lethal element, the classic poison of detective fiction.

clue.text: Note added by station hand

parts.note: a post is a station, such as a sentry's position
script means handwriting, a person's hand

explanation.surface: A railway station worker adding a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' suggests a worker, but it means handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A postscript is the extra message written at the end of a letter after the signature.

clue.text: Prudish play on words about girl in film

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a play on words goes round the girl

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
Rita is the girl in the film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A straitlaced reaction to a joke about an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a 1983 British film about a working-class woman who goes to university.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is someone with strict moral views, and the word is used as an adjective for prudish.

clue.text: Go without love, with girls getting visual aids

indicators.note: without means minus, so a letter is taken out of the word go

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Someone without a partner going out with girls and needing spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the O (love, zero in tennis), leaving G. 'Go without love' reads as being single, which hides the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses are spectacles, lenses worn to help the eyes see.

clue.text: Tough, but Hansard, alas, is wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests something in error, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that the official parliamentary record is unfortunately inaccurate.
explanation.walkthrough: Hansard is the official verbatim record of UK parliamentary debates. 'is' looks like the verb before 'wrong', but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extremely resilient and unfeeling, a strong way of calling someone tough.

clue.text: He's now setting out terms of endearment

indicators.note: out means in disarray, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of he's, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man who is now laying out his pet names for a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting out' looks like one indicator, but 'setting' is fodder and only 'out' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the affectionate, meaningless words lovers murmur to each other.

clue.text: Activist from new aircrew room ejecting male

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A protester comes out of a recently built aircrew lounge after throwing a man out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejecting' says the M for 'male' is thrown out of the pooled letters before 'new' rearranges the rest, so the leftover ten letters make the activist.
explanation.definitionFit: An eco-warrior is a campaigner who takes direct action to protect the environment.

clue.text: Source of liquidity remains fluid in milk supplier

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the word for the milk supplier

parts.note: a cow supplies milk
ash is what remains after burning
FL is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz

explanation.surface: Liquid leftovers poured into a dairy cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of liquidity' looks literal beside 'fluid' and 'milk', but liquidity here is the financial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash flow is the money moving through a business, which is what keeps it liquid in financial terms.

clue.text: Sort of bullet for people in case of terror

indicators.note: in puts the word for people inside the outer letters
case of means the outside casing, the first and last letters of terror

parts.note: a race is a people

explanation.surface: A kind of ammunition designed to cause terror among a population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of terror' keeps its outer letters, T and R, with RACE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer bullet burns as it flies, so its path can be seen and the aim corrected.

clue.text: Usual practice with university learner pinching answer

parts.note: a habit is a regular practice

indicators.note: pinching means gripping, so the letters for university and learner hold the letter for answer

parts.note: L is the learner sign on a British car

explanation.surface: A student at university routinely nicking the answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like stealing, but it puts A between U and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual describes something done regularly by habit, the same as usual or customary.

clue.text: Women's organisation call for the work of an electrician

parts.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A women's group phoning to book an electrician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a long-established British organisation for women, known for jam and community activities.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiring is the system of electric cables in a building, which an electrician installs.

clue.text: Formulas for fixing prices inclusive of energy!

indicators.note: inclusive of means taking in, so the reworked letters contain the letter for energy
fixing suggests repairing or adjusting, so the letters of prices are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Price-fixing rules that include energy bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing prices' makes RCIPES, and 'inclusive of' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipes are sets of instructions for making something, and formulas are the same thing in a technical sense.

clue.text: A member on line by toilet area gets light

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so the member with its article follows the line

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is a toilet
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician standing in a queue next to the toilets is getting illuminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in an across clue means coming after, and 'by' is only a link, so the toilet and area pieces lead and the member ends the word, against the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A lava lamp is a decorative light in which coloured wax rises and falls in liquid.

clue.text: Phenomenal returns providing growth

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the letters run in the reverse direction
providing means supplying from within, so the letters come from inside phenomenal

explanation.surface: Remarkable profits that supply economic growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phenomenal returns' reads as huge profits, but the answer sits backwards inside 'Phenomenal'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anemone is a flowering plant, and plants are growth in the botanical sense.

clue.text: Brain surgery that's required by astronaut?

definitions.meaning: like brain surgery, this is a byword for an intellectually demanding task, as in it's not brain surgery
the study of rocket propulsion is literally what space flight depends on

explanation.definitionFit: Rocket science is both a byword for something very hard and the real engineering behind spaceflight.

clue.text: Expanse of blubber under lass's rear

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the word for blubber below the letter from lass
rear means back end, picking the final letter of lass's

parts.note: to blubber is to weep noisily

explanation.surface: A girl crying hard over her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like the noun for whale fat, but it is the verb for crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is a wide stretch of land or water, an expanse.

clue.text: Bellies up in filth

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: tums is a childish word for bellies

explanation.surface: Stomachs turned up in the dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TUMS upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is soot or dirt, and also obscene material, filth in both senses.

clue.text: Blockage, but almost got by after motorway backed up

indicators.note: after puts the word for got by behind the reversed motorway
backed up means turned back, so the motorway letters are reversed

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written here as MI

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: passed means got by, as in overtook

explanation.surface: A traffic jam on the motorway that you nearly managed to get round.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is London's motorway to the north, written MI in crosswords; 'backed up' turns it to IM. 'almost' takes the D off PASSED.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock or situation with no way through, a blockage.

clue.text: Always the same gear?

definitions.meaning: outfit or clothing, here the standard dress worn by a group

explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means consistent and unchanging, and it is also the regulation clothing of a group.

clue.text: Right hand clenches while disregarding danger

indicators.note: clenches means grips tightly, so the outer letters hold the word for while

parts.note: as can mean while, as in as he spoke

explanation.surface: A fist clenched in a moment of recklessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clenches' looks like a fist, but it puts AS between R and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means acting hastily without thinking about the risks.

clue.text: Newly-trained pet so clean and shiny?

indicators.note: newly trained suggests something reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recently house-trained pet stays clean and glossy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shiny?' is a loose definition, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Opalescent means showing a milky, shifting iridescence like an opal, a kind of sheen.
